MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MAY 22, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:12 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Traffic Engineer Joanne Itagaki
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION – MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS

  Mayor Huff presented a proclamation in support of Maternal Mental Health Awareness
  proclaiming May as Maternal Mental Health Awareness Month. Councilmember Schmitz
  shared her experience with a maternal mental health disorder and stressed the
  importance of mental health resources and a strong support team. Dr. Carol Berkowitz,
  a pediatrician Harbor-UCLA and Dr. Ellie Handler, Chair of LA County Perinatal Mental
  Health Task Force were present to accept the Proclamation.

B.  PROCLAMATION – OLDER AMERICANS MONTH: ENGAGE AT EVERY AGE

  Mayor Huff presented a proclamation in support of Older Americans Month encouraging
  older adults to engage at every age.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 22, 2018
 5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL requested that ITEM 5G* be removed from the Consent
  Calendar for individual consideration. There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-F AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 24, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS –APRIL AND MAY 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 59959 THROUGH 59984 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $75,271.78; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040118 THROUGH 040718;
  59765 THROUGH 59772; 59800 THROUGH 59814; 59815 THROUGH 59818
  (VOID); 59839 (VOID); 59840 (VOID); AND 59869 THROUGH 59887 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $229,130.35 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $304,402.13
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  APRIL 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  APRIL 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 23, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 22, 2018
 G.*  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 7, 2018

  Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell commented that during the Planning Commission’s
  consideration of Planning Application No. 19-15 there was considerable discussion
  concerning the proposed revised home designs for the Chandler Ranch project and there
  were some very close votes for the revised designs. She further commented that these
  are new designs that the City Council has not seen and it may be worthwhile for the
  City Council to take the matter under consideration.

  Planning Director Wahba commented that there are three sets of homes designs in the
  project - A, B and C; and Toll Brothers has purchased the “B” plan (30 homes) and is
  proposing the revised home designs. He further noted that there are still three designs
  being reviewed.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO AGENDIZE THE DESIGN REVIEW
  OF THE PLAN B HOMES IN PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-15 (RESIDENCES
  AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB) FOR CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION
  AFTER THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S FINAL REVIEW OF THE REVISED
  DESIGNS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF MAY 7, 2018

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  Gayle Barney, 7 Silver Bit Lane expressed concern regarding an increased number of
  peafowl in the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates neighborhood. She requested that the
  City Council consider a budget allocation to provide for trapping and removing/relocating
  large numbers of peafowl and consider amending the ordinance that protects peafowl in
  the Dapplegray Lanes neighborhood.

  Following an explanation of the City’s current policy on peafowl, an overview of the lengthy
  history of this matter and brief discussion, the following direction was given to staff:

  STAFF WAS DIRECTED TO ASSIST THE HOA WITH CONTACTS AND
  INFORMATIONAL RESOURCES FOR COORDINATING A HOA/PROPERTY OWNER
  FUNDED PEAFOWL TRAPPING PROGRAM.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 22, 2018
 7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

NONE.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB/CHANDLER RANCH
  ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the stop limit striping changes on
  Chandler Ranch Road at Palos Verdes Drive East as shown in Exhibit A.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a staff report (as per agenda material). She
  also noted that removing a portion of the three-rail fencing was considered but doing so
  would not increase visibility at the intersection.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S question regarding the impact actual
  speed, rather than posted speed, has on sight distance, Traffic Engineer Itagaki
  commented that, while increased speed does require longer sight distance, she would
  need to consult speed studies specific to this location to provide an informed opinion in
  this case.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she visited the site and she believes the
  proposed changes are an appropriate solution. She suggested that staff monitor the
  intersection for traffic accidents and revisit later if necessary.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE STOP LIMIT STRIPING CHANGES ON
  CHANDLER RANCH ROAD AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AS SHOWN IN
  EXHIBIT A AS RECOMMENDED

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 22, 2018
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports
  to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently active
  Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special
  districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various committees on which Members of the City
  Council might serve or have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

MAYOR HUFF thanked the Equestrian Committee, staff and the entire equestrian community
for their efforts in organizing a very successful Mayor’s Ride on May 5. She also provided a
brief summary of several recent events including the Chamber’s Salute to Business Luncheon,
where Kathy Gould, PVLD Director was awarded the Brunning Leadership Award; the CCCA
Annual Municipal Seminar; and the Coyote Watch trainings that took place in April/May.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed disappointment in the turnout at the candidate’s
forum hosted by the Chamber.

MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL noted that in May she attend the City Selection Committee
meeting at which a new LAFCO Commissioner and several County library seats were filled. She
further noted that she also attended the SCAG General Assembly meeting where a bylaw
amendment to allow past presidents to serve an additional five year term on the Regional
Council was voted down.

MAYOR HUFF also provided an overview of the recent developments in the Susan Leeds
homicide investigation.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:18 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of George
  Deukmejian, Larry Clark and Susan Leeds.

  An adjourned meeting of the City Council will be held on June 6, 2018 at 8:00 a.m. in
  the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California for the purpose of conducting a Budget Study Session.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 22, 2018
   The next regular meeting of the City Council will be held on Tuesday, June 12, 2018 at
  7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes
  Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 22, 2018
